text:
sam: heads-up — noticed in eu-west the autoscaler keeps adding c5d-large nodes instead of GPU pools when training jobs spike. pods pending for ~3m, autoscaler picks binpack-like candidate and ends up with wrong instance type. anyone seen this pattern?

maya: yup, saw that during the retrain yesterday. cluster-autoscaler expander seems to prefer "least-waste" and our GPU pools are slightly overcommitted with taints so CA avoids them. quick fix was to relax taints but that's not ideal for isolation.

aaron: can you paste the CA args from the deploy? also which node groups are defined — are GPUs in a separate node group with correct capacity-type label?

sam: here's the arg block from our helm values:

```
        - --cloud-provider=aws
        - --expander=least-waste
        - --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
        - --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
        - --balance-similar-node-groups
        - --max-empty-bulk-delete=10
```

sam: GPU pools are labelled `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: g5.12x` and tainted `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule`. Pods have tolerations but scheduler prefers cheaper non-gpu nodes because binpacking/least-waste calculation thinks the small CPU-only nodes are a better fit for pending resource requests (our training pods request flexible CPU but ask for gpu via nodeSelector).

zhen: two ideas: 1) try `--expander=most-pods` or `--expander=price` to see different behavior; 2) use node group priorities via nodeGroupPriorityExpander (policy file) so GPU node groups get higher priority when GPU is requested. We added a priority policy at another company and it helped avoid wrong pool selection.

maya: agree on policy file. also we can reduce `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to be more aggressive on removing cheap nodes, prevents packing many tiny nodes that preclude GPU choices. but careful — aggressive scale-down with spot instances can thrash.

aaron: what about marking GPU node groups with a stronger selector like `kubernetes.io/arch=gpu` and set pod `nodeSelector`/`affinity` so the scheduler prefers them earlier? That pushes the scheduling decision before CA selection.

sam: good call. another axis: provisioning time for GPU instances is currently ~120s vs 30s for cpu nodes in eu-west. CA picks fastest-to-provision to satisfy most pods quicker. We could add a provisioning penalty to cheaper pools by using a custom expander policy that multiplies score by estimated boot time.

zhen: example priority policy snippet we used: (policy JSON loaded via `--expander=policy`):

```
{
  "priorities": [
    {"name": "gpu-priority", "nodeGroup": "ng-gpu-*-g5", "weight": 100},
    {"name": "spot-penalty", "nodeGroup": "ng-spot-*", "weight": -20}
  ]
}
```

zhen: CA will then favor `ng-gpu-*` for matching pods. obviously adjust names.

maya: cost note — adding priority means more on-demand GPU nodes, increases $$. Might be ok short term; we should pair with a reserved capacity plan for critical training windows.

aaron: ops checklist I'd propose: 1) switch to policy expander in staging and add GPU weight, 2) tighten pod affinity/nodeSelector for confirmed GPU workloads, 3) reduce `scale-down-unneeded-time` to 5m in staging, 4) monitor scale-up latency and boot times, 5) consider mixing instance types in GPU node group to allow smaller cheaper GPUs.

sam: OK I'll test `--expander=policy` in staging with a conservative policy and post back metrics. infra-bot will log the rollout.

infra-bot: Deploy started: cluster-autoscaler/staging -> image v1.22.3, args updated to `--expander=policy`. Rolling restart in progress. :rocket:

maya: thanks — also can we add a prometheus alert if CA picks non-gpu pool while there are pending pods with gpu requests for >90s? would catch regressions.

aaron: yeah I'll add an alert rule: `sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests_gpu) by (cluster) - sum(kube_node_labels{label="gpu"})` ish — will craft proper query.

sam: awesome. I'll share results and a short runbook for when this happens in prod. :+1:
